findings.title: The optimized audit-log paginator cannot handle datetime keys
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key passes the AuditLogEntry datetime to math.floor/math.ceil, which raises TypeError. Consequently, an authorized user's optimized_pagination=true request fails whenever results are nonempty. value_from_cursor also returns a numeric value instead of converting it to a datetime. This paginator needs the datetime conversions provided by DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Django querysets do not support negative slicing
findings.body: When advanced features are enabled and a supplied cursor has a negative offset, this branch slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start. Django raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.") rather than handling the boundary automatically. Thus the advertised negative-offset feature produces a server error on the optimized audit-log endpoint. Reject invalid offsets with a pagination error or implement reverse traversal without negative queryset indices.

findings.title: Changing existing Redis keys from sets to sorted sets requires a migration
findings.body: The buffer now uses ZADD and ZSCAN on the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous version populated with SADD. Any buffered segment present during deployment remains a Redis set, so new insertions and flushing those segments fail with WRONGTYPE. Mixed-version consumers also cannot read or write each other's buffers. Provide a compatible conversion or a versioned-key rollout that drains the old buffers before switching; otherwise deployment stalls processing of existing data.

findings.title: Unioning sorted sets must preserve timestamps rather than sum them
findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM. A replayed span can exist both in the destination buffer and in a newly staged parent buffer when that parent has already been redirected. Merging those buffers doubles the duplicate payload's end-timestamp score, although its actual timestamp has not changed. Subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction then retains these replayed old spans ahead of genuinely newer spans. Use an aggregation mode such as MAX so merging duplicate payloads preserves their timestamp.

findings.title: Insertion eviction ignores the configured segment span limit
findings.body: SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, but the Python span-count check was removed and this script unconditionally caps every segment at 1000. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments exceeding that limit, while a larger configured limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit to the insertion script and use it for eviction, or explicitly remove the configurable contract rather than leaving it ineffective.
